body:
⚠️ Trap carried in from #12232's dev report — read before starting this card.

`apps/docs/app/page.tsx` is a **shadowed route**: `proxy.ts` rewrites `/` to `/en`, so `RootPage()` never runs (measured: `curl /` returns `200 text/html`, not the 307 that file would produce). Filed standalone as #12255.

What it means here: the homepage's real metadata lives in `apps/docs/app/[lang]/page.tsx`. An agent that adds JSON-LD to `app/page.tsx` will ship a green PR that changes nothing served. Verify against a rendered response, not against the file you edited.

The epic does not depend on #12255 being fixed — it stays a standalone finding — but this card does depend on knowing about it.

Claim: PM loop round 5 (epic PM for #12243)
Session: `session_f9f0958b-ab68-46cc-801c-216aa7ee2107`
Branch: `claude/issue-12240-json-ld`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-12240`
Domain: `domain:devx`
File surface: `apps/docs/app/[lang]/page.tsx`, `apps/docs/app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`, `apps/docs/app/[lang]/blog/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — no path-derived mandate
Clause-②: no
Serial constraints cleared: PR #12325 (Open Graph) merged as `c48d46d70`, releasing these three files. #12242 stays queued BEHIND this card: it shares `app/[lang]/page.tsx` and the blog page, and it now also owns hoisting the `/hero-cover-dark.png` literal into `lib/site.ts`.

⚠️ Standing condition for this round: production has not deployed since ~16:55 today (#12333), so **nothing merged after that point can be verified against the live site**. Verify against a local production build (`next build && next start`), and do not treat the live site as evidence for or against your change.

Dev claim (os-dev subagent under the epic PM session, dispatched for this card)

- Session: `session_f9f0958b-ab68-46cc-801c-216aa7ee2107`
- Branch: `claude/issue-12240-json-ld` (pushed empty at `cf99875ea` before the first edit — write-route probe green)
- Worktree: `/Users/zhuangjianguo/Documents/GitHub/objectstack-issue-12240`
- Base: `cf99875ea88a6a611353442e76c93de70727b74d`
- File surface: `apps/docs/app/[lang]/page.tsx`, `apps/docs/app/[lang]/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`, `apps/docs/app/[lang]/blog/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`

Standing conditions acknowledged: `app/page.tsx` is shadowed (#12255) — the served homepage is `app/[lang]/page.tsx`; production has not deployed since ~16:55 (#12333), so verification is against a local `next build && next start` only.

**ACCEPT** — PR #12355, 4 files, +405/-2. The surface expansion is accepted; the reasoning below.

**My assumption 2 was partly falsified, and the response to that is the best thing in this report.** `source.pageTree` does carry an ancestor chain, but for 17 of the 35 `meta.json` files the ancestor arrives with a **name and no `url`** — fumadocs attaches a folder's `index.mdx` as `folder.index` only when `meta.json` does *not* list `"index"` in `pages`. So 172 of 403 doc pages ship a trail that skips its own section. Google requires `item` on every crumb but the last.

The dispatch said that if the tree did not give the chain cleanly, the finding was worth more than a hand-rolled fallback. **It did not build the fallback.** It filed #12352 with an ablation instead — and the ablation is causal, not correlational: it deleted one `"index"` entry from `data-modeling/meta.json`, **rebuilt**, and watched `/docs/data-modeling/objects` go from 3 crumbs to 4 while an untouched control section stayed at 3. When #12352 lands, the trails complete with no code change here. A consumer-side URL reconstruction would have made a content-config defect permanent and invisible, which is exactly what this repo's contract-first directive forbids.

**`dateModified` is not a second source of truth** — `lib/structured-data.tsx` calls `app/sitemap.ts`'s own default export once per process and indexes the result, so the JSON-LD value and the `<lastmod>` are the same object serialised twice. Byte-equal on all 406 dated pages, checked. That was a hard constraint in the dispatch and it was met by construction rather than by coincidence.

**`SoftwareSourceCode` over `SoftwareApplication`, and the reason is right**: Google's Software App rich result *requires* `offers` / `aggregateRating` / `review`, so a `SoftwareApplication` node would report missing-required errors in the very validator the card's acceptance names — for a rich result this project can never be eligible for.

**Validation claimed accurately.** Google's Rich Results Test was **not** run and is not claimed — it needs a public URL and this branch is not deployed (and production is pinned, #12333). Instead all 408 pages were checked field by field against schema.org ranges and Google's documented required properties: 407 carry a block, 0 failures, and the assertions include the ones that actually bite — no raw `<` surviving into the payload, every `{"@id"}` reference resolving inside its own `@graph`, breadcrumb positions contiguous from 1, `license` as the Apache-2.0 **URL** because schema.org's `license` ranges over `CreativeWork|URL` and not `Text`. The blog index emits nothing, stated plainly rather than left to be discovered.

**Surface expansion accepted.** A fourth file, `lib/structured-data.tsx`, beyond the three page routes I declared — for one `Organization` identity instead of three copies, and one copy of the `</script>` escaping instead of three. Contention was checked *before* writing it (no open PR touched `apps/docs` at that moment), which is the part that makes a declared expansion safe rather than merely announced.

**A build break found inside the branch, and named rather than buried**: a comments-only commit broke the build, because a comment containing the glob `content/docs/**/meta.json` closes the block comment at `*/` — 18 `tsc` syntax errors. Caught only because the gate union was re-run on a commit that "was just comments". Worth its own line in this repo, which already carries an ESLint rule for the sibling failure (an *unterminated* block comment swallowing code); this is the mirror image — a comment that terminates *early*.

**A hypothesis of the dev's own that did not hold, recorded rather than dropped**: it expected the 17 folder-index pages to be navigation orphans too. Crawling all 408 sitemap URLs for inbound links found 4 orphans, none of them folder indexes (#12353).

⚠️ **One thing this PR ships that is inherited-wrong, and the fix belongs elsewhere**: `codeRepository` reads `https://github.com/objectstack-ai/framework`, from `gitConfig` in `lib/layout.shared.tsx`. I verified it: `objectstack-ai/framework` and `objectstack-ai/objectstack` return the **same repository id** (`1136691870`), so it is a rename redirect. Every nav link, hero button and edit link already rides that redirect, and now a machine-readable identity claim does too. ⛔ Not a local override here — fixing `gitConfig` fixes all of them at the producer, which is #12354. Promoting it now.
